Hi Ben / Monica,

Attached are Aperture's consolidated redlines to the DPA and a short spreadsheet showing the fields we need captured on the Order Form (data residency, subprocessors, KMS preference). A couple of quick items we want to surface before legal starts formal negotiations: 

- SCCs: we see two points where Redwood's language implies hosting in the US as a fallback. We need to confirm whether execution of the EU Commission SCCs will be sufficient for our EU hosts, and whether a transfer-impact addendum is planned if US-based processing happens.
- Controller/Processor roles: the draft has some language that is ambiguous on whether certain telemetry/aggregation functions are considered \"processing for Redwood's legitimate interests\" vs. \"processing on behalf of Aperture\". We need clarity and preferably explicit role delegation sections for logs and monitoring.
- Order Form: For Regulated Submissions we require a field indicating whether Private deployment or Dedicated capacity is used. Please see the attached OrderForm_Schedule.xlsx for our preferred fields.

We're aiming for an internal decision by the week of 13 May; can you confirm whether Redwood legal can review and provide an initial comments matrix within 5 business days of receiving our tracked redline doc?

Hi Elena, Ben — thanks for the redline and the spreadsheet. A few operational clarifications so legal can scope edits: 

1) Logs/Telemetry: by default Redwood retains platform-level logs for 30 days for operational diagnostics; we can provide export snapshots or a dedicated log export for customers on Dedicated/Private deployments. For Hosted, we can include a logs export deliverable in the Order Form (requires procurement approval).

2) KMS: we support customer-managed keys for Dedicated and Private but not for our thin-hosted tier. If Aperture needs KMS for Hosted, we'd need to look at a configuration and pricing addendum.

3) Subprocessors: the redline looks like it expects a full subprocessor inventory on signature. Our standard approach is a categorized list in the DPA and a quarterly inventory feed for enterprise customers. If Aperture requires signature-time disclosure of every subprocessor, that will be a deviation and we'll flag it in redlines.

I'll consolidate these operational points into a short "ops note" to attach to the redline and hand to Marissa/Legal to respond to the contract items.

Monica
Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Elena — thanks for the clear tracker and the expectation callout. Ben/Monica, I reviewed the redline and have three legal tracks below; I've also attached a comments matrix that maps Aperture's asks to our standard positions. 

1) Transfer-addendum + SCCs: Redwood can commit to executing the EU Commission SCCs between controller/processor as appropriate. For Hosted fallbacks to US processing, we will offer the standard transfer-impact addendum language that includes our risk-mitigation summary. Aperture's redline requests an explicit promise to not transfer backup snapshots outside the EU without notice — we can agree to notice plus a 30-day cure period before any cross-border move, unless required by law.

2) Roles / logs: propose this language for Section 2.1 (Roles): "Redwood acts as processor for Customer data, except for aggregated telemetry used solely for service improvement and platform security, which Redwood may process as controller after pseudonymization." We'll offer a short ops exhibit that limits retention and exportability of raw logs for Hosted customers.

3) Subprocessors: we can provide an initial signature-time categorized list and commit to 30 days' notice for material changes. Signature-time disclosure of every vendor will be an exception; if Aperture insists, that will be a procurement redline.

Next steps: Elena, please let us know which items are non-negotiable for Aperture (SCC wording, backup residency, KMS requirement). Ben — can you confirm whether Aperture is targeting Dedicated or Private for the pilot? If Private/Dedicated, we can accept stronger KMS and signature-time subprocessor requirements with an order-form commitment.

I'll attach the comments matrix and send to Elena as tracked changes in the next message.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
VP, Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
